title: 2009 USAMO Problem 4
statement:
For \(n \ge 2\) let \(a_1\), \(a_2\), ..., \(a_n\) be positive real numbers such that

\[
(a_1+a_2+ ... +a_n)\left( {1 \over a_1} + {1 \over a_2} + ... +{1 \over a_n} \right) \le \left(n+ {1 \over 2} \right) ^2
\]

Prove that \(\text{max}(a_1, a_2, ... ,a_n) \le 4 \text{min}(a_1, a_2, ... , a_n)\).

solutions.text:
Assume without loss of generality that $a_1 \geq a_2 \geq \cdots \geq a_n$. Now we seek to prove that $a_1 \le 4a_n$.
By the Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality, \begin{align*} (a_n+a_2+ a_3 + ... +a_{n-1}+a_1)\left({1 \over a_1} + {1 \over a_2} + ... +{1 \over a_n}\right) &\ge \left( \sqrt{a_n \over a_1} + n-2 + \sqrt{a_1 \over a_n} \right)^2 \\ (n+ {1 \over 2})^2 &\ge \left( \sqrt{a_n \over a_1} + n-2 + \sqrt{a_1 \over a_n} \right)^2 \\ n+ {1 \over 2} &\ge n-2 + \sqrt{a_n \over a_1} + \sqrt{a_1 \over a_n} \\ {5 \over 2} &\ge \sqrt{a_n \over a_1} + \sqrt{a_1 \over a_n} \\ {17 \over 4} &\ge {a_n \over a_1} + {a_1 \over a_n} \\ 0 &\ge (a_1 - 4a_n)\left(a_1 - {a_n \over 4}\right) \end{align*}
Since $a_1 \ge a_n$, clearly $(a_1 - {a_n \over 4}) > 0$, dividing yields:
\[0 \ge (a_1 - 4a_n) \Longrightarrow 4a_n \ge a_1\]
as desired.
